assumptions: The protease's cleavage rules are PeptideCutter's or the RPG grammar given.
Complete digestion with the missed cleavages allowed.
limits: In-silico: digestion efficiency, modifications and detectability are not predicted.
The MS window filters what an instrument would see, it does not predict intensity.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which peptides, masses and m/z values does a proteolytic digest of this protein give?

description: In-silico proteolytic digest of a protein (ExPASy PeptideCutter / PeptideMass): peptides with coordinates, average and monoisotopic masses, m/z per charge state, and the MS mass-window filter. 49 proteases and chemicals — or an enzyme of your own written in RPG rule grammar — one or several at a time; a multi-enzyme digest runs concurrently (all at once, products re-digested until nothing changes) or sequentially (one result per enzyme).

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

charges.description: charge states to report m/z for, e.g. [1,2,3] — [M+zH]z+ from the monoisotopic mass.

customCleave.description: cleaving rules for the 'custom' enzyme, in RPG grammar: the comma is the cut, so '(,A)' cleaves before A and '(K or R,)' after K or R. Empty parentheses mean any residue.

customExceptions.description: exceptions for the 'custom' enzyme; each must repeat the rule it blocks, e.g. '(K or R,)(P)' = not when P follows.

customRegex.description: the 'custom' enzyme as a regular expression instead of RPG grammar (pyteomics' `rule=`): it matches at P1 and the cut falls after the match, e.g. '[KR]' cleaves after K or R. Single-enzyme only, and mutually exclusive with `customCleave`. Advanced.

cysteine.description: cysteine alkylation applied before the digest, as ExPASy PeptideMass offers it. Mass deltas are Unimod's.

enzyme.description: protease or chemical (single-enzyme digest), or 'custom' to use `customCleave`. Values: arg-c (Arg-C proteinase), asp-n (Asp-N endopeptidase), asp-n-sg (Asp-N, sequencing grade (D and C)), bnps-skatole (BNPS-Skatole), bromelain (Bromelain), caspase-1 (Caspase 1), caspase-10 (Caspase 10), caspase-2 (Caspase 2), caspase-3 (Caspase 3), caspase-4 (Caspase 4), caspase-5 (Caspase 5), caspase-6 (Caspase 6), caspase-7 (Caspase 7), caspase-8 (Caspase 8), caspase-9 (Caspase 9), chymotrypsin-high (Chymotrypsin (high specificity)), chymotrypsin-low (Chymotrypsin (low specificity)), clostripain (Clostripain (Arg-C)), cnbr (CNBr), elastase (Elastase), enterokinase (Enterokinase), factor-xa (Factor Xa), ficin (Ficin), formic-acid (Formic acid), glu-c (Glu-C (D and E)), glutamyl-endopeptidase (Glutamyl endopeptidase), granzyme-b (Granzyme B), hydroxylamine (Hydroxylamine), iodosobenzoic-acid (Iodosobenzoic acid), lysc (Lys-C), lysn (Lys-N), lysarginase (LysargiNase), neutrophil-elastase (Neutrophil elastase), ntcb (NTCB (2-nitro-5-thiocyanobenzoic acid)), papain (Papain), pepsin-ph2.0 (Pepsin (pH > 2)), pepsin-ph1.3 (Pepsin (pH 1.3)), proalanase (ProAlanase), proline-endopeptidase (Proline endopeptidase), proteinase-k (Proteinase K), staph-peptidase-i (Staphylococcal peptidase I), tev (TEV protease (Tobacco Etch Virus)), thermolysin (Thermolysin), thrombin (Thrombin), thrombin-sg (Thrombin (sequencing grade)), trypsin (Trypsin), trypsin-low (Trypsin (low specificity)), trypsin-simple (Trypsin (simple K/R)), alp (α-lytic protease (aLP)), custom (Custom cleavage rule).

enzymes.description: two or more proteases for a multi-enzyme digest; overrides `enzyme`. Order matters in concurrent mode. 'custom' takes its place in the order like any other.

keilExceptions.description: apply Keil's exception rules (sites trypsin does NOT cut despite matching). Only defined for trypsin. PeptideCutter and Bioconductor cleaver apply these by default, which is why this does too; pyteomics does not, so turn it off to cross-check against pyteomics.

massMax.description: keep only peptides at or below this monoisotopic mass [Da]; omit for no upper bound.

massMin.description: keep only peptides at or above this monoisotopic mass [Da]; omit for no lower bound.

metOxidation.description: methionine oxidation. 'all' oxidises every Met (masses move, peptide list unchanged); 'both' lists each Met peptide TWICE, unmodified and oxidised, as PeptideMass does.

missedCleavages.description: single enzyme: allow up to this many internal sites per peptide (pyteomics). Multi-enzyme: append runs of up to this many merged adjacent peptides (RPG).

mode.description: multi-enzyme only. 'concurrent' = all at once, re-digesting products until nothing changes (can cut where no single enzyme cuts the intact chain); 'sequential' = one result per enzyme, each on the intact protein.

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

semi.description: also emit semi-enzymatic peptides (one ragged terminus).

name: protein_digest

count.description: peptides returned after any mass filter

coverage.description: fraction of the protein covered by the peptides returned

peptides.description: peptides with start/end, sequence, missed cleavages, masses and m/z (all results pooled in multi-enzyme mode)

results.description: multi-enzyme only: one entry per digestion (per enzyme in sequential mode, one for the whole set in concurrent), each with its own peptides, sites and coverage

sites.description: cleavage-site positions (0-based residue index the next peptide starts at)

totalPeptides.description: peptides the digest produced BEFORE the mass filter
